# Example results (generated by scripts/generate_examples.py)

Default parameters: B₀ = 0.3 T, N = 200, v = 1 m/s, A = 0.005 m² (a = 3.99 cm), θ = 0°, start 30 cm, magnet passes through the coil, N pole facing, R = 10 Ω.

## Default run

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Peak positive EMF | 0.8135 V |
| Peak negative EMF | -0.8135 V |
| Maximum \|current\| | 81.352 mA |
| Maximum flux per turn | 188.995 µWb |
| Average EMF (−NΔΦ/Δt) | 0.0000 V (flux returns to its start value) |
| Mean \|EMF\| while moving | 0.1257 V |

## Experiment A: peak EMF vs B_ref

| B_ref | Peak \|EMF\| (V) | \|EMF\|/B_ref |
|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | 0.27117 | 2.71172 |
| 0.2 | 0.54234 | 2.71172 |
| 0.4 | 1.08469 | 2.71172 |
| 0.6 | 1.62703 | 2.71172 |
| 0.8 | 2.16938 | 2.71172 |
| 1 | 2.71172 | 2.71172 |

### Experiment A

When B₀ increased from 0.1 to 1 T (×10.00), the peak EMF changed from 271.2 mV to 2.712 V (×10.00).

Theory predicts peak EMF ∝ B₀. Fit through the origin: ε_peak = 2.712·B₀ with R² = 1.000000; the ratio ε_peak/B₀ varies by only 0.000 %. Result: consistent with direct proportionality. A stronger magnet scales the field everywhere by the same factor, so the flux Φ(x) and its rate of change dΦ/dt scale with B₀.

### Experiment B

When N increased from 50 to 1000 turns (×20.00), the peak EMF changed from 203.4 mV to 4.068 V (×20.00).

Theory predicts peak EMF ∝ N. Fit through the origin: ε_peak = 0.004068·N with R² = 1.000000; the ratio ε_peak/N varies by only 0.000 %. Result: consistent with direct proportionality. Each turn links the same flux, so the total flux linkage NΦ — and therefore ε = −N dΦ/dt — is proportional to N.

### Experiment C

When v increased from 0.25 to 5 m/s (×20.00), the peak EMF changed from 203.4 mV to 4.068 V (×20.00).

Theory predicts peak EMF ∝ v. Fit through the origin: ε_peak = 0.8135·v with R² = 1.000000; the ratio ε_peak/v varies by only 0.000 %. Result: consistent with direct proportionality. On the same path, the flux depends only on position: dΦ/dt = (dΦ/dx)·v. Doubling v halves the time for the same flux change, doubling the EMF.

## Experiment D: Lenz's law

| Case | Dominant EMF (V) | Current seen from magnet | Coil face | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| N pole approaches | -0.6950 | anticlockwise | N | repels, opposing the approach |
| N pole moves away | +0.6950 | clockwise | S | attracts, opposing the separation |
| S pole approaches | +0.6950 | clockwise | S | repels, opposing the approach |
| S pole moves away | -0.6950 | anticlockwise | N | attracts, opposing the separation |
